(p. 351)

Surah 39, verse 1: *"The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise."*

Survey (istiqra') of the Mighty Qur'an (the method of inductively examining its texts) has shown that Allah, Exalted and Majestic is He, whenever He mentions the sending down of His Book, follows that with some of His Most Beautiful Names, which comprise His Sublime Attributes.

At the beginning of this noble surah, when He mentioned the sending down of His Book, He made clear that the origin of its sending down is from Him, Exalted and Majestic is He. He mentioned His Name Allah, His Name al-'Azīz (the Mighty), and al-Ḥakīm (the Wise). He mentioned the same at the beginning of Surah al-Jāthiyah, in His saying: ﴿Ḥā Mīm. The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise. Indeed, in the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers﴾ [al-Jāthiyah: 1–3]. And at the beginning of Surah al-Aḥqāf, in His saying: ﴿Ḥā Mīm. The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise. We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth﴾, and so on [al-Aḥqāf: 1–3].

Mentioning some of His names and attributes after the mention of the sending down of the Qur'an has occurred frequently in the Qur'an, such as:

• His saying at the beginning of the surah: ﴿Ḥā Mīm. The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the All-Knowing. Forgiver of sin, Acceptor of repentance, Severe in punishment, Possessor of abundance. There is no deity except Him; to Him is the final return﴾ [Ghāfir: 1–3].

• His saying at the beginning of Fuṣṣilat: ﴿Ḥā Mīm. A revelation from the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 1–2].

• His saying at the beginning of Hūd: ﴿Alif Lām Rā. A Book whose verses are perfected and then detailed from one who is Wise and Acquainted﴾ [Hūd: 1].

• His saying in Fuṣṣilat: ﴿And indeed, it is a mighty Book. Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or behind it; it is a revelation from the Wise, the Praiseworthy﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 41–42].

• His saying at the opening of Yā-Sīn: ﴿A revelation of the Mighty, the Merciful﴾ ﴿to warn a people whose fathers had not been warned﴾ [Yā-Sīn: 5–6].

• His saying: ﴿And indeed, it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. The Trustworthy Spirit brought it down﴾, and so on [al-Shu'arā': 192–193].

• His saying: ﴿A revelation from the Lord of the worlds. And if he had made up about Us some sayings﴾, and so on [al-Ḥāqqah: 43–44].

It is not hidden that His mention of these Great and Most Beautiful Names after His mention of the sending down of this Mighty Qur'an clearly indicates the greatness of the Mighty Qur'an, the sublimity of its status, and the importance of its revelation (p. 352), and Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 2:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So worship Allah, making the religion sincerely His﴾ ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah belongs sincere devotion (al-din al-khalis)﴾. Allah, majestic and exalted, commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) in this noble verse that he worship Him, being one who makes the religion sincerely His, meaning sincere to Him in His worship, free from all kinds of shirk, minor and major, as is clear from the wording of the verse.

Ikhlas (sincerity) is singling out the one worshipped with intention, in everything He has commanded us to draw near to Him by. What this noble verse includes, that sincerity in worship belongs to Allah alone and is indispensable, has come in several verses. Allah, majestic and exalted, has also made clear that He has not commanded any act of worship except the worship in which the worshipper is sincere to Him.

As for the one who is not sincere, everything of that kind he does comes from his own initiative, not by the command of his Lord. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, making the religion sincerely His﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 5], and Allah, majestic and exalted, said: ﴿Say, "Indeed, I have been commanded to worship Allah, making the religion sincerely my own. And I have been commanded to be the first of the Muslims."﴾ up to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "It is Allah I worship, making my religion sincerely His. So worship what you will besides Him."﴾ [az-Zumar: 14, 15].

We have already discussed righteous deeds and that they must be accompanied by sincerity, at the beginning of Surat al-Kahf, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds﴾ up to the end of the verse, and in other places besides that.

As for His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse: ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah belongs sincere devotion﴾, meaning: pure monotheism, free from the taints of shirk; that is, He alone is the one deserving of it, and He is the One who commanded it.

The saying of some scholars that the intended meaning of "sincere devotion" is the statement "There is no god but Allah" is consistent with what we have mentioned. And Allah, exalted is He, knows best.

Then, when Allah, majestic and exalted, mentioned the sincerity of worship to Him alone, He clarified the doubt of the disbelievers by which they argued for associating others with Him, exalted is He, in

The statement of Allah the Exalted here: ﴿And those who take protectors besides Him, [saying], "We worship them only that they may bring us near to Allah in position."﴾ So He made clear that they claim they worshipped the idols only so that they would bring them close to Allah in position. The word *zulfa* (nearness, closeness in rank) means kinship or closeness.

Thus His saying *zulfa* stands in place of the absolute object (*mutlaq*, a verbal noun that emphasizes or specifies the action) implied by His saying *liyuqarribūnā* (that they may bring us near). That is, that they may bring us near to Him in a nearness by which their intercession benefits us, in their claim.

For this reason they used to say in their talbiyah (the invocation of the pilgrimage): "Here I am, O Allah, You have no partner, except a partner who is Yours; You own him and what he owns."

We have already mentioned, in the discussion of His saying in Surat al-Ma'idah, ﴿And seek the means of approach to Him﴾ [al-An'am: 35], that this kind of claiming intercessors, and taking worshipped beings other than Allah as intermediaries, is among the roots of the disbelief of the disbelievers.

Allah has explicitly stated this in Surat Yunus, in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And they worship besides Allah that which neither harms them nor benefits them, and they say, "These are our intercessors with Allah." Say, "Do you inform Allah of something He does not know in the heavens or on the earth?" Glorified is He and exalted above what they associate with Him﴾ [Yunus: 18].

So He explicitly stated that this kind of claiming intercessors is shirk (association of partners with Allah), and He declared His noble self free of it by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Glorified is He and exalted above what they associate with Him﴾. He alluded to this in this verse of Az-Zumar. For when He said about them, ﴿We worship them only that they may bring us near to Allah in position. Indeed, Allah will judge between them concerning that over which they differ﴾ [az-Zumar: 3], He followed that with His saying, ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a liar and [a] disbeliever﴾ [az-Zumar: 3].

His saying *kaffār* (disbeliever) is an intensive form (*sigha mubalagha*, a form denoting emphasis or intensity), which indicates that those who said "We worship them only that they may bring us near to Allah in position" combine in that statement both lying and extreme disbelief. Further clarification of this will come, Allah willing, in the discussion of Surat an-Nas.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 4:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Had Allah wished to take a son, He would have chosen whatever He willed from what He creates. Glory be to Him! He is Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾ We have already presented, at great length, the clarifying verses in Surah an-Nahl, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they assign to Allah daughters, glory be to Him, while for themselves is what they desire﴾ [an-Nahl: 57].

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 6:**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He created you from a single soul, then made from it its mate﴾. In this noble verse, He, majestic and exalted, mentions that He created the children of Adam from a single soul, which is their father Adam (p-354), then made from that soul its mate, meaning Eve. That is: He dispersed all the children of Adam from the two of them. He clarified this in other places of His Book, such as His saying, exalted is He, at the beginning of Surat an-Nisa': ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul and created from it its mate and dispersed from both of them many men and women﴾ [an-Nisa': 1], and His saying in al-A'raf: ﴿It is He who created you from one soul and made from it its mate that he might find comfort in her﴾ to the end of the verse [al-A'raf: 189]. The feminine form of the adjective, in His words "single" (wahidah), though the thing described is masculine, namely Adam, is according to the feminine grammatical gender of the word "soul" (nafs), even though it refers to a male. A parallel to this in Arabic speech is the saying of the poet:

"Your father is a caliph, whom another (woman) bore, and you are the caliph of that perfection."

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He sent down for you of the cattle eight pairs﴾. We have previously explained these eight pairs by the explicit text of the Mighty Qur'an, in Surat Al 'Imran, in discussing His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And horses branded, and cattle and tillage﴾ [Al 'Imran: 14].

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, within three darknesses﴾. We have previously mentioned the verses that clarify this in Surat al-Hajj, in discussing His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then indeed We created you from dust﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Hajj: 5], and we explained there the meaning of the three darknesses mentioned here.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 7:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿If you disbelieve, then indeed Allah is Free of need from you﴾. In this noble verse, Allah, Mighty and Exalted, has made clear that He is absolutely free of need from His creation (al-ghina al-mutlaq), and that their disbelief in Him does not harm Him. The verses that clarify this meaning are numerous, such as:

• His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And Moses said: If you disbelieve, you and whoever is on earth entirely, then indeed Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy﴾ [Ibrahim: 8].

• His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So they disbelieved and turned away, and Allah was self-sufficient, and Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy﴾ [At-Taghabun: 6].

• His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They say: Allah has taken a son. Glory be to Him! He is the Free of need﴾, and the verse [Yunus: 68].

• His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O mankind, you are the poor toward Allah, and Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy﴾ [Fatir: 15].

• His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And Allah is the Free of need, while you are the poor﴾ [Muhammad: 38].

We have clarified this with verses in several places in this blessed Book.

* *

(p-355) The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return﴾. We have already presented its explanation, along with the removal of the difficulty and the answer to the questions raised concerning those verses, in surah Bani Isra'il, in the discussion of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another, and We would not punish until We sent a messenger﴾ [Al-Isra': 15]. We also clarified that, along with the removal of the difficulty in some verses, in surah An-Nahl, in the discussion of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That they will bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection and of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge﴾, and the verse [An-Nahl: 25].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 8:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him in repentance; then when He bestows upon him a favor from Himself, he forgets what he had been calling upon Him for before, and he sets up rivals to Allah in order to lead [others] astray from His way.﴾ We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah Yunus, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, whether lying on his side, or sitting, or standing﴾ [Yunus: 12], the verse.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Enjoy your disbelief for a little while; indeed, you are of the companions of the Fire.﴾ We have already presented the verses that clarify it, along with a reference to the study of its principles (usul) in Surah al-Hijr, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Leave them to eat and enjoy themselves, and let hope distract them; but they will soon know﴾ [al-Hijr: 3].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 10:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah's earth is spacious﴾. The apparent meaning of the verse is that if a person is in a place where he cannot establish his religion in the required manner, then he must emigrate from it, "into the vast expanses of Allah's spacious earth," until he finds a place where he is able to establish his religion.

He, may He be exalted, has clarified this meaning in other places, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves, the angels will say, "In what [condition] were you?" They will say, "We were oppressed in the land." The angels will say, "Was not the earth of Allah spacious that you could have emigrated therein?"﴾ [An-Nisa: 97]. And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O My servants who have believed, indeed My earth is spacious, so worship only Me﴾ [Al-Ankabut: 56]. And it is not hidden that the sequence marked by the particle fa' (ف, "so") in His saying ﴿so worship only Me﴾ after His saying ﴿indeed My earth is spacious﴾ is a clear proof of this.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 15:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, that is the manifest loss.﴾

(p-356) We have already presented the verses that clarify this matter, from several aspects, in surah Yunus, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Certainly, they have lost who denied the meeting with Allah, and they were not guided.﴾ [Yunus: 45].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 16:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿For them there will be layers of fire above them, and beneath them layers.﴾ ﴿That is what Allah uses to frighten His servants.﴾ We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surat al-Anbiya', in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If only those who disbelieved knew the time when they will not be able to avert the Fire from their faces or from their backs﴾ [al-Anbiya': 39], and we mentioned a portion of that in Surat Bani Isra'il, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers﴾ [al-Isra': 8].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 17:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who avoided the false deities (ṭāghūt), not worshipping them, and turned penitently to Allah﴾. What this noble verse includes of the realization of the meaning of "There is no god but Allah" (lā ilāha illā Allāh), we have already explained with Qur'anic verses in Surah al-Fatiha, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿You alone we worship﴾ [al-Fatiha: 5].

The commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 18:

Allah's statement: ﴿Those who listen to the word and follow the best of it﴾. The most evident of the opinions regarding this noble verse is that "the word" refers to what the Prophet (ﷺ) brought of the revelation of the Book and the Sunnah. Among the uses of "word" for the Qur'an is Allah's statement: ﴿Do they not ponder the word?﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 68], and His statement: ﴿Indeed, it is a decisive word, and it is not a jest﴾ [al-Tariq: 13-14]. As for His statement in this noble verse: ﴿then they follow the best of it﴾ [al-Zumar: 18], it means that they give precedence to the best, which is more excellent in goodness, over the good that is lesser in goodness, and they give precedence to the best absolutely over the merely good. Verses from the Book of Allah support this.

As for the evidence that the best word to be followed is what was revealed to him (ﷺ) of the revelation, it is found in verses of the Book of Allah, such as His statement: ﴿And follow the best of what has been sent down to you from your Lord﴾ [al-Zumar: 55], and His statement to Musa, commanding him to take the best of what is in the Torah: ﴿So take hold of it with strength and command your people to take the best of it﴾ [al-A'raf: 145].

As for the Qur'an containing the best (al-ahsan) and the good (al-hasan), verses of His Book have indicated this.

Know first that there is no doubt that the obligatory (al-wajib) is better than the recommended (al-mandub), and that the recommended is better than the merely permissible good (mutlaq al-hasan). So when they hear, for example, His statement: ﴿And do good, that you may succeed﴾ [al-Hajj: 77], they give precedence to the obligatory good over the recommended good, and they give precedence to the latter over the merely good, which is the permissible (al-ja'iz). For this reason, the reward is specifically for the best, which is the obligatory and the recommended, and not for the merely good, as He said: ﴿And We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do﴾ [al-Nahl: 97], and He said: ﴿And He will reward them with the best of what they used to do﴾ [al-Zumar: 35]. We have already clarified this in the commentary on Surah al-Nahl, in the discussion of His statement: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while being a believer - We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do﴾ [al-Nahl: 97]. There we also explained the indication of the verses that the permissible is good, as the author of al-Maraqi said:

"What our Lord has not forbidden is good, and what is other than it is ugly and abhorrent."

Among the examples of encouragement to take the best and its superiority, while permitting taking the good, is His statement: ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished. But if you are patient, it is better for the patient﴾ [al-Nahl: 126]. The command in His statement ﴿then punish with the like of that with which you were punished﴾ is for permissibility, and Allah does not command except what is good. This indicates that retaliation is good, but Allah has explained that pardon and patience are better than it and superior to it, in His statement: ﴿But if you are patient, it is better for the patient.﴾ Similar examples are numerous in the Qur'an, such as His statement regarding the permissibility of retaliation: ﴿And whoever avenges himself after being wronged - those have no blame upon them﴾ [al-Shura: 41], together with His clarification that patience and forgiveness are better than it, in His statement after it: ﴿And whoever is patient and forgives - indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination﴾ [al-Shura: 43]. And like His statement regarding the permissibility of retaliation: ﴿Allah does not like the public mention of evil speech except by one who has been wronged﴾ [al-Nisa': 148], although He pointed out that pardon is better than it, and that it is among His attributes, exalted is He, despite His complete power, in His statement after it: ﴿If you disclose a good deed or conceal it or pardon an offense, indeed Allah is ever Pardoning and Competent﴾ [al-Nisa': 149]. And like His statement, exalted is He, praising the one who gives charity and displays it: ﴿If you disclose your charities, then how excellent they are﴾ [al-Baqarah: 271], then He clarified that concealing them and giving them to the poor is better than displaying them, the display which He praised with the rigid verb, which is used to create praise, namely ni'imma, in His statement: ﴿If you disclose your charities, then how excellent they are; but if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 271].

And like His statement regarding half of the obligatory dowry for the wife upon divorce before consummation: ﴿then half of what you have specified﴾ [al-Baqarah: 237]. There is no doubt that each of the spouses taking half is good, because Allah prescribed it in His Book in His statement: ﴿then half of what you have specified.﴾ Yet He encouraged each of them to forgive the other half of his share, and He clarified that this is closer to piety, in His statement after it: ﴿And that you forgive is closer to righteousness. And do not forget graciousness between you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 237].

Allah has said: ﴿And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it﴾ [al-Shura: 40], then He guided to the best in His statement: ﴿But whoever pardons and makes reconciliation - his reward is upon Allah﴾ [al-Shura: 40]. And He said: ﴿And for wounds is retribution﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 45], then He guided to the best in His statement: ﴿But whoever gives it as charity, it is an expiation for him﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 45].

Know that concerning this noble verse there are opinions other than the one we have chosen.

Among them is what was narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding the meaning of ﴿then they follow the best of it﴾: he said, "It is the man who hears the good and the ugly, so he speaks of the good and refrains from the ugly, so he does not speak of it."

It was also said: they listen to the Qur'an and other than it, then they follow the Qur'an.

It was also said: the intended meaning of "the best word" is "There is no deity except Allah." Some who hold this view say that the verse was revealed concerning those who believed in Allah before the sending of the Messenger (ﷺ), such as Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Nufayl al-'Adawi, Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, Salman al-Farisi, and others besides them among the opinions.

Concerning His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Is then one against whom the word of punishment has been decreed [able to be saved]? Could you then rescue one who is in the Fire?﴾ The more apparent of the two views regarding this noble verse is that they are two independent sentences. His saying ﴿Is then one against whom the word of punishment has been decreed﴾ is an independent sentence, but within it there is an ellipsis (ḥadhf), and the omission of what the context indicates is clear and presents no difficulty.

The estimated meaning (taqdīr) is: "Is then one against whom the word of punishment has been decreed [one whom] you can deliver from it?" The interrogative carries the meaning of negation, i.e., you, O Prophet of Allah, cannot deliver anyone whom Allah has foreknown in His knowledge to punish with that punishment. This omitted element is indicated by His saying after it, ﴿Could you then rescue one who is in the Fire?﴾

We have previously mentioned several times the two views of the exegetes concerning the interrogative particle combined with a conjunctive particle such as the fā' (then) and the wāw, and thumma (then), as in His saying here, ﴿Is then one [against whom]...﴾ and His saying ﴿Could you then rescue...﴾

As for the view that the speech is a single conditional sentence, as al-Zamakhsharī said: the original form of the speech is "Is it that one against whom the word of punishment has been decreed, so you rescue him?" — a conditional sentence into which the interrogative hamzah of denial has entered, with the fā' being the fā' of the apodosis; then the fā' that is at its beginning entered for coordination upon an omitted element indicated by the address, its estimate being: "Are you the master of their affair, so that whoever the punishment has been decreed upon, you rescue him?" The second hamzah is the first one, repeated to emphasize the meaning of denial and remoteness, and placing "whoever is in the Fire" in the position of the pronoun. Accordingly, the verse on this view is a single sentence; but it does not appear fully clear.

Know that what this noble verse indicates has already been explained by us, with Qur'anic verses, at the beginning of Surah Yā-Sīn, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Certainly the word has come into effect upon most of them﴾ [Yā-Sīn: 7], and we showed how the verses indicate the intended meaning of "the word of punishment."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 20:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But those who fear their Lord will have elevated chambers, above which are built chambers﴾. What this noble verse contains, of the promise to the people of Paradise of built chambers, He, majestic and exalted, mentioned in other than this place,

• such as His saying, exalted is He, in Surah Saba': ﴿Except one who believes and does righteousness; for those, there will be a double reward for what they did, and they will be in the upper chambers, secure﴾ [Saba': 37].

• And His saying, exalted is He, in Surah al-Tawbah: ﴿Allah has promised the believing men and believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein, and pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence﴾ [al-Tawbah: 72], to the end of the verse.

• And His saying, exalted is He, in Surah al-Saff: ﴿He will forgive you your sins and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow and pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence. That is the great achievement﴾ [al-Saff: 12]. Because the pleasant dwellings mentioned in al-Tawbah and al-Saff are inclusive of the chambers mentioned in al-Zumar and Saba', and we have already presented a portion of this in Surah al-Furqan, in discussing His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those will be rewarded with the chamber for what they patiently endured﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Furqan: 75].

**Al-Shinqiti's commentary (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 39, verse 21:**

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky and makes it flow as springs in the earth?﴾. *Yanabi'* (springs) is the plural of *yanbu'*, which means a large quantity of water.

His saying, *fasalakahu* (and makes it flow), means *adkhalahu* (He causes it to enter). As we have already explained, with its Arabic evidences and the Qur'anic verses, in Surat Hud, in the discussion of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿We said: Carry in it two of every kind, a pair﴾ and the rest of the verse [Hud: 40].

(p-360) What this noble verse of Surat al-Zumar contains, we have clarified at the beginning of Surat Saba', in the discussion of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He knows what enters into the earth and what comes out of it﴾ and the rest of the verse [Saba': 2].

* *

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then He brings forth thereby crops of varying colours﴾. We have already discussed what resembles this among the verses in Surat al-Rum, in the discussion of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the differences of your languages and your colours﴾ [al-Rum: 22]. We also referred to it in Surat Fatir, in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and We bring forth thereby fruits of varying colours?﴾ and the rest of the verse [Fatir: 27].

* *

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then it dries up and you see it turning yellow; then He makes it into debris. Indeed in that is a reminder for people of understanding﴾.

His saying, ﴿Then it dries up﴾, means: then, after the freshness and greenness of that crop, it withers, its drying is completed, and it is uprooted from its place, so you, O observer, see it yellow and dry, its greenness and freshness gone. ﴿Then He makes it into debris﴾ means into crumbs, broken, dry stalks, scattered by the winds. ﴿Indeed in that﴾, that which has been mentioned of the states of that crop, with its varying colours, ﴿is a reminder﴾, that is, a lesson, an admonition and a reminder ﴿for people of understanding﴾, that is, for those whose minds are sound and free from the flaws of defect. Exalted and Most High has mentioned the fate of this crop by way of admonition and reminder. He has also explained in another place that what He admonished His creatures with here, concerning the states of this crop, is likewise a likeness of the worldly life. So He admonished with it in one place and used it as a likeness of the state of the world in another place. This is in His saying, Exalted is He, in Surat al-Hadid: ﴿Know that the life of this world is only play and amusement, adornment and boasting among you, and rivalry in wealth and children, like the likeness of rain whose vegetation pleases the disbelievers; then it dries up and you see it turning yellow; then it becomes debris﴾ [al-Hadid: 20]. And in Surat al-Rum, He clarifies that among the causes of its turning yellow is the sending of the wind upon it, in His saying: ﴿And if We sent a wind and they saw it turning yellow, they would certainly continue to disbelieve after it﴾ [al-Rum: 51].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 22:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Is one whose breast Allah has expanded to Islam, so that he is upon a light from his Lord...?﴾ The discussion of this has already preceded in Surat al-An'am, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Whomever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam﴾ [al-An'am: 125].

(p-361) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whomever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾. We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah an-Nahl, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If you are eager for their guidance, indeed Allah does not guide those who lead astray﴾ [an-Nahl: 37], and elsewhere in that passage.

Allah's saying: ﴿An Arabic Qur'an, without any crookedness﴾. We have already presented the verses clarifying this in the beginning of Surat al-Kahf, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿And He did not make for it any crookedness; [but has made it] straight﴾ [al-Kahf: 1-2]. As for His saying in this noble verse, "Qur'anan" is in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial qualifier), and it is an emphatic ḥāl; the actual ḥāl is "ʿarabiyyan," and "Qur'anan" serves as a preparatory introduction to it (tawṭi'a). It has also been said that it is in the accusative as a madḥ (laudatory accusative).

His saying in this noble verse, "ʿarabiyyan," means: because it is in the Arabic tongue (lisān ʿarabī), as He said: ﴿The tongue of the one they point to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue﴾ [al-Naḥl: 103]. He said at the beginning of Surat Yūsuf: ﴿Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an, so that you may reason﴾ [Yūsuf: 2 – as cited by the author], and He said at the beginning of al-Zukhruf: ﴿Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an, so that you may reason﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 3]. He said in Ṭā-Hā: ﴿And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an, and We have variously presented in it of the warning, so that they may fear Allah, or it may produce for them a remembrance﴾ [Ṭā-Hā: 113]. And He said in Fuṣṣilat: ﴿And if We had made it a non-Arabic Qur'an, they would have said, "Why have its verses not been detailed? Is it non-Arabic and Arabic?"﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 44]. And He said in al-Shuʿarāʾ: ﴿And indeed, it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down upon your heart, that you may be among the warners, in a clear Arabic tongue﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 192-195]. And He said in Surat al-Shūrā: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you an Arabic Qur'an, that you may warn the Mother of Cities and those around it﴾ [al-Shūrā: 7], and so on, through other verses.

And in al-Raʿd He said: ﴿And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic judgment. And if you were to follow their desires after the knowledge that has come to you, you would have from Allah no protector or defender﴾ [al-Raʿd: 37].

These Qur'anic verses indicate the nobility and greatness of the Arabic language, an indication that none denies except an obstinate person.

(p-٣٦٢) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And he who brings the truth﴾. Allah, glorified and exalted, made clear that the *alladhi* (the relative pronoun "who," singular) in this verse carries the meaning of *alladhina* (the plural "those who"), as evidenced by His following words: ﴿Those are the God-fearing. For them is whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the reward of the good-doers﴾ [al-Zumar 39:33–34; the verse cited as al-'Ankabut: 33–34 in the source].

We have mentioned in other places that *alladhi* comes with the meaning of *alladhina* in the Qur'an and in the speech of the Arabs. Among its examples in the Qur'an is His saying, exalted be He, in this verse of al-Zumar: ﴿And he who brings the truth﴾, and the verse. And His saying, exalted be He, in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿Their likeness is like the likeness of one who kindled a fire﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:17], meaning: those who kindled a fire, as evidenced by His following words: ﴿Allah took away their light and left them in darkness, not seeing﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:17].

• And His saying in it also: ﴿like one who spends his wealth to be seen by the people﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:264], meaning: like those who spend, as evidenced by His following words: ﴿They have no power over anything of what they have earned﴾, and the verse.

• And His saying, exalted be He, in al-Tawbah: ﴿and you plunged in as those before you plunged﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:69].

This is according to the view that *alladhi* is a relative pronoun (*mawsulah*), not a verbal-noun particle (*masdariyyah*, a particle that forms a verbal-noun clause with the following verb). A parallel to this in the speech of the Arabs is the saying of Ashhab ibn Rumaylah:

*And indeed those whose blood was spilled at Falj, they are the people, the whole people, O Umm Khalid.*

And the saying of 'Udayl ibn al-Farkh al-'Ijli:

*So I spent the night giving drink to the people, my brothers, those whose error is error and whose right guidance is right guidance.*

And the saying of the rajaz poet:

*O Lord of Abs, do not bless any of them,*
*neither the one who stood among them nor the one who sat,*
*except those who stood at the edges of the palm-fiber.*

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in *Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab* (Removing the Illusion of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book):

(p-٣٨٠) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surat al-Zumar.

His saying, exalted be He: ﴿And he who brings the truth﴾.

It is apparent in the singular.

And His saying: ﴿Those are the God-fearing﴾ [al-Zumar 39:33] indicates otherwise. We have already presented the aspect of the plural, examined in detail with its evidences, in Surat al-Baqarah, in the discussion of His saying, exalted be He: ﴿Their likeness is like the likeness of one who kindled a fire﴾, and the verse [al-Baqarah 2:17].

His statement, the Exalted: ﴿For them there is whatever they wish with their Lord; that is the reward of the doers of good﴾. We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surat an-Nahl, in the discussion of His statement, the Exalted: ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence which they will enter, beneath which rivers flow; for them therein is whatever they wish﴾ [an-Nahl: 31].

﴿And He will reward them with the best of what they used to do.﴾ We have already mentioned the verses that clarify this in this noble surah, in the discussion of His saying, ﴿So give good tidings to My servants, who listen to the word and follow the best of it﴾ [Al-Zumar: 17–18]. (p-363) And in Surat al-Nahl, in the discussion of His saying, ﴿And We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do﴾ [Al-Nahl: 97].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 36:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Is not Allah sufficient for His servant?﴾. We have already presented the verses that clarify it in Surah al-Anfal, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O Prophet, Allah is sufficient for you and for those of the believers who follow you﴾ [al-Anfal: 64]. According to the reading of the majority, ﴿bi-kāfin ʿabdahu﴾ is with a fatḥah on the ʿayn and a sukūn on the bāʾ, with the word ʿabd in the singular, and what is meant by it is the Prophet ﷺ. This is like His saying: ﴿So Allah will suffice you against them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 137], and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O Prophet, Allah is sufficient for you﴾ [al-Anfal: 64], and the verse that follows it.

As for the reading of Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī, ʿibādahu, with a kasrah on the ʿayn and a fatḥah on the bāʾ followed by an alif, as the plural of ʿabd, the apparent meaning is that it includes the righteous servants of Allah among the prophets and their followers.

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they frighten you with those besides Him﴾. In this noble verse, He, majestic and exalted, mentioned that the disbelievers, the worshippers of idols, frighten the Prophet ﷺ with the idols they worship besides Allah, because they say to him: indeed, they will harm him and afflict him with madness. This is the custom of the idol-worshippers, may Allah curse them: they frighten the messengers with idols, and they claim that they will harm them and reach them with evil.

It is well known that the prophets of Allah, upon them be the blessings and peace of Allah, do not fear anything other than Allah, especially idols, which do not hear or see, and neither harm nor benefit. For this reason, Allah, the Exalted, said about His prophet Ibrahim when they frightened him with them: ﴿How should I fear what you associate, when you do not fear that you associate with Allah that for which He has not sent down to you any authority? So which of the two parties is more worthy of security?﴾ [al-An'am: 81], and the verse.

He also said about His prophet Hud, and what his people said to him of that kind: ﴿We say nothing except that some of our gods have struck you with evil.﴾ He said: ﴿Indeed, I call Allah to witness, and bear witness that I am free from what you associate with Him, besides Him. So plot against me all together, then give me no respite. Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds its forelock. Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path.﴾ [Hud: 54–56].

He said in this noble surah, addressing our Prophet ﷺ after mentioning their frightening him with their idols: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "Allah." Say, "Have you considered what you invoke besides Allah? If Allah intended for me some harm, could they remove His harm? Or if He intended for me mercy, could they withhold His mercy?" Say, "Sufficient for me is Allah. Upon Him rely the reliant."﴾ [al-Zumar: 38].

It is well known that fear of those idols is among the most heinous forms of disbelief and associating partners with Allah.

Allah, the Exalted, has also explained in another place that Satan frightens the believers too, those who are followers of the messengers, from among his followers and allies among the disbelievers, as He said: ﴿That is only Satan frightening his allies, so do not fear them, but fear Me, if you are believers.﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 175].

The more apparent view is that in His saying ﴿frightening His allies﴾ the first object has been omitted, meaning: he frightens you with his allies, as evidenced by His saying after it: ﴿so do not fear them, but fear Me﴾, and the verse.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 38:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Have you considered what you invoke besides Allah? If Allah should intend me some harm, are they removers of His harm? Or if He intends me mercy, are they withholders of His mercy?﴾

What Allah, exalted and most high, mentioned in this noble verse, namely that the things worshipped besides Him cannot remove a harm which Allah intends for anyone, nor withhold a mercy which He intends for anyone, has been explained in many verses,

such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Why do you worship that which neither hears nor sees, and which avails you nothing?﴾ [Maryam: 42]

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said: Do they hear you when you call? Or do they benefit you or harm you? They said: Rather, we found our fathers doing thus.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 72-74]

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whatever mercy Allah grants to people, none can withhold it; and whatever He withholds, none can release after Him. And He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.﴾ [Fatir: 2]

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if Allah touches you with harm, there is no remover of it except Him; and if He intends you good, there is no repeller of His bounty. He causes it to reach whom He wills of His servants.﴾ [Yunus: 107] and the verse continues.

Verses of this kind are many and well known.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 45:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter recoil; but when those other than Him are mentioned, behold, they rejoice.﴾ We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surat as-Saffat, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, that is how We deal with the criminals. Indeed, they, when it was said to them, "There is no deity except Allah," were arrogant.﴾ [Saba': 35].

The Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 39, verse 47:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if those who did wrong had everything on earth and the like of it with it, they would surely offer it as ransom from the terrible punishment on the Day of Resurrection.﴾ (p-365) In this noble verse, exalted and majestic is He, mentions that those who did wrong, namely the disbelievers, if they had in the Hereafter everything on earth and the like of it with it, they would ransom themselves with it from the terrible punishment that they witnessed on the Day of Resurrection. He clarified this meaning in other places and stated explicitly in them that there is absolutely no ransom on the Day of Resurrection.

- Like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers, never will be accepted from any of them the earth filled with gold even if he were to ransom himself by it. For those is a painful punishment, and they will have no helpers.﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 91].

- And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, even if they had everything on earth and the like of it with it to ransom themselves thereby from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it would not be accepted from them, and for them is a painful punishment. They will want to leave the Fire, but they will not be emerging from it, and for them is an enduring punishment.﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 36-37].

- And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So today no ransom will be taken from you or from those who disbelieved. Your refuge is the Fire; it is more worthy of you, and wretched is the destination.﴾ [al-Hadid: 15].

- And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if they should offer every ransom, it would not be accepted from them. Those are the ones who were given up to what they had earned. For them is a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment because they used to disbelieve.﴾ [al-An'am: 70].

- And His saying: ﴿And if they should offer every ransom﴾, meaning: and if they should offer every ransom (fida'),

- And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And no ransom will be accepted from it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 48], the verse.

- And His saying: ﴿Nor will ransom be accepted from it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 123], and 'adl means ransom (fida').

- And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who did not respond to Him, if they had everything on earth and the like of it with it, they would surely offer it as ransom. Those will have the evil of the account, and their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting place.﴾ [al-Ra'd: 18].

We have already presented a portion of this in Surah Aal 'Imran, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Never will be accepted from any of them the earth filled with gold even if he were to ransom himself by it﴾, the verse [Aal 'Imran: 91].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 48:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And there will become apparent to them the evils of what they had earned﴾. His saying: ﴿And there became apparent to them﴾ means: there became apparent to them the evils of what they had earned, i.e., the recompense of their evil deeds which they had acquired in the world. The apparent meaning is that He used "evils" here while intending by them their recompense.

Its parallel in the Qur'an is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it﴾ [al-Shura: 40].

Similar to this also is the use of "punishment" (ʿiqab) for the recompense of punishment, in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿That is so. And whoever retaliates with the like of what he was harmed with and then is oppressed - Allah will surely support him﴾ [al-Hajj: 60], to the end of the verse.

And what this noble verse includes, that they will have revealed to them on the Day of Resurrection the reality of what they used to do in the world, has been clarified in other verses, such as:

• His saying, the Exalted: ﴿There every soul will know what it had sent before﴾ [10:30].

• His saying, the Exalted: ﴿On that Day man will be informed of what he sent ahead and kept back﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 13].

• His saying, the Exalted: ﴿A soul will know what it has presented and what it has kept back﴾ [al-Infitar: 5].

• His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They will say, "Woe to us! What is this book that leaves nothing small or great but has enumerated it?" And they will find what they did present, [all] there﴾ [al-Kahf: 49], to the end of the verse.

• His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And every person We have fastened his bird [i.e., deeds] to his neck, and We will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection a record he will find spread open. "Read your record. Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as an accountant"﴾ [al-Isra: 13-14].

And other verses besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 49:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So when adversity touches man, he calls upon Us; then when We bestow upon him a favor from Us, he says, "I was only given it because of knowledge."﴾ We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah Yunus, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when adversity touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side﴾ [Yunus: 12], and so on.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 53:

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab [Removing the Appearance of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book]):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah﴾, the verse.

This noble verse indicates two matters:

The first: that those who commit excess (al-musrifun) are not permitted to despair of the mercy of Allah. Yet there is a verse indicating the opposite, namely His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And that the transgressors (al-musrifun) are the companions of the Fire﴾ [Ghafir: 43].

The answer is that excess (al-israf) may be by disbelief, and it may be by committing sins short of disbelief. So the verse ﴿And that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire﴾ refers to the excess that is disbelief.

And the verse ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves﴾ refers to excess by sins short of disbelief. It may also be answered that the verse ﴿And that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire﴾ applies if they do not repent, and His saying ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed﴾ applies if they repent.

The second matter: that it indicates the forgiveness of all sins, yet other verses indicate that there are sins which are not forgiven, namely associating partners with Allah, exalted is He.

The answer is that the verse ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him﴾ [An-Nisa: 48] specifies this verse (takhsis). Some scholars said: this verse is restricted by repentance, based on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And turn in repentance to your Lord﴾ (p-381) [Az-Zumar: 54], for it is conjoined to His saying ﴿do not despair﴾ [Az-Zumar: 53]; and on this basis there is no difficulty. This is the view preferred by Ibn Kathir.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 55:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And follow the best of what has been sent down to you from your Lord﴾. We have already presented the verses that clarify this in this noble surah, in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So give good tidings to My servants who listen to the word and follow the best of it﴾ [az-Zumar: 17-18]. And we presented a portion of it in Surah an-Nahl, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do﴾ [an-Nahl: 97].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 58:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or [lest] one should say, when he sees the punishment, "If only I had another turn [in the world], I would be among the doers of good."﴾ We have already presented the verses clarifying this from several aspects in Surat al-A'raf, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿On the Day its interpretation comes, those who had forgotten it before will say, "The messengers of our Lord had certainly come with the truth. So do we have any intercessors to intercede for us, or could we be returned so that we might do other than what we used to do?"﴾ [al-A'raf: 53].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 60:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about Allah, their faces blackened﴾. We have already presented the discussion of it, and of the similar verses, in surah Aal 'Imran, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿On the Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 106] and what follows it.

* *

(p-367) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Is there not in Hell an abode for the arrogant?﴾

Its explanation has already been presented with Qur'anic verses, together with a statement of several of the evil effects of arrogance (kibr), in surah al-A'raf, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He said, "Then descend from it; it is not for you to be arrogant therein, so get out. Indeed, you are among the debased"﴾ [al-A'raf: 13].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 65:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it has already been revealed to you and to those before you: "If you associate partners with Allah, your deeds will surely be nullified."﴾ The discussion of this has already preceded in Surah al-An'am, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if they had associated others with Allah, what they used to do would have been nullified for them.﴾ [al-An'am: 88].

We have also mentioned in Surah al-Ma'idah the verse that contains the qualification which is not mentioned in these verses, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever disbelieves in the faith, his deeds have certainly become void﴾ — the verse [al-Ma'idah: 5].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 68:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then it will be blown again, and behold, they will be standing, looking on﴾. We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah Ya-Sin, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the Horn will be blown, and behold, from their graves they will hasten to their Lord﴾ [Ya-Sin: 51].

This is the commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 69:

Allah's words: ﴿And the Book will be placed﴾. We have already explained this, with Qur'anic evidence, in surah al-Kahf, in the discussion of His words: ﴿And the Book will be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it﴾ [al-Kahf: 49], and in surah Bani Isra'il, in the discussion of His words: ﴿And We will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection a book which he will find spread open﴾ [al-Isra': 13].

* *

Allah's words: ﴿And the prophets and the witnesses will be brought, and judgment will be made between them with truth, and they will not be wronged﴾ ﴿And every soul will be paid in full for what it did﴾. The scholars differed concerning the meaning of "the witnesses" (al-shuhada', plural of shahid) in this noble verse. Some of them said: they are the guardian angels who used to record their deeds in the worldly life. Whoever said this relied on His words: ﴿And every soul will come, with it a driver and a witness﴾ [Qaf: 21].

Some scholars said: the witnesses are the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ), who will bear witness over the nations, as He said: ﴿And thus We have made you a middle nation, that you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger a witness over you﴾. (p-368) It was also said: the witnesses are those who were killed in the way of Allah. The most apparent of the sayings concerning the verse, in my view, is that the witnesses are the messengers from among mankind, who were sent to the nations, because judgment is not passed between a nation until its messenger comes, as Allah explicitly stated in surah Yunus in His words: ﴿And for every nation there is a messenger; when their messenger comes, judgment is made between them with justice, and they will not be wronged﴾ [Yunus: 47]. So He, exalted is He, explicitly stated that He will question the messengers about what their nations answered them with, as He said: ﴿On the Day when Allah will gather the messengers and say, "What was your response?"﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 109], and He said: ﴿So We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent, and We will surely question the messengers﴾ [al-A'raf: 6]. His words may also allude to this: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness and bring you against these as a witness?﴾ [al-Nisa': 41], because his being (ﷺ) the witness over those who are his Ummah indicates that the witness over every nation is its messenger.

He, exalted is He, has also made clear that the witness over every nation is from among the nation's own selves, and this shows that it is not from the angels. This is in His words: ﴿And on the Day We raise up in every nation a witness against them from among themselves﴾ [al-Nahl: 89]. The messengers are from among the selves of their nations, as He said of our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿There has certainly come to you a messenger from among yourselves﴾ [al-Tawbah: 128]. And He said: ﴿Allah has certainly conferred favour upon the believers when He sent among them a messenger from among themselves﴾, the verse [Al 'Imran: 164].

The justification for the brevity by omitting the subject in His words: ﴿And those who were brought﴾ [al-Zumar: 69] — i.e., ﴿And the prophets were brought﴾ — is that it is among what is known and undisputed that none can bring them except Allah alone, exalted is He.

The reading of this letter (the verb) by the majority of the Seven, other than al-Kisa'i and Hisham on the authority of Ibn 'Amir, is ﴿wujii'a﴾ with a pure kasrah on the jim (wujiʼa, with clear i-vowel).

Al-Kisa'i and Hisham, on the authority of Ibn 'Amir, read it with ishmam of the kasrah toward the dammah (a slight rounding of the lips, signalling the u-sound while keeping the i-form).

The ishmam here is permissible, and the kasrah is permissible as well, because no confusion at all arises in the verse between the active and the passive voice. It is known that His words here, "wujii'a" (was brought), are in the passive voice and cannot be taken as active in any way. Whatever is like this allows both the pure kasrah and the ishmam of the kasrah toward the dammah, as he indicated in the Khulasah (Ibn Malik's poetic summary of grammar) with his words:

"Pronounce with kasrah or ishmam the triliteral verb whose middle radical is weak, and whose first radical takes damma as in buʻa (was sold), and it is admitted."

(p-369) As for when this verb is attributed to a suffixed pronoun of the nominative, that may lead to confusion, so the passive is confused with the active. In that case it is necessary to avoid the form that causes confusion and to use what removes the confusion, whether by vowel-marking or ishmam, as he indicated in the Khulasah with his words:

"If a vowel-marking causes fear of confusion, it is to be avoided."

An example of this is the line of the poet, which Ibn Manzur (author of Lisan al-'Arab) cited:

"And I am, toward the patron, though his benefit is small, one who repels when I am wronged, not patient under it."

His words "dumtu" (I was wronged) originally were "dimtu" in the passive, so either ishmam or damma is required, because a pure kasrah would make it admit of being active, as in "bi'tu" and "sirtu". And the words of Jarir lamenting al-Marrar ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakrah:

"And I say, from grief, when we were tried by him, and my tears in my cloak are abundant:
For the burying ones, the brother of nobility and generosity, by Allah, what the stones have covered (ḍumina) through you!"

Its original form is "fūtnā" in the passive, so either kasrah or ishmam is required, because a pure damma would make it admit of being active, as in "qulna" and "qumna".

The Almighty's saying: ﴿And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups﴾ [al-Zumar 71]. *Al-zumar* are the scattered companies; its singular is *zumrah*. Here He, exalted is He, described them as *zumar*. In al-Mulk He described them as *afwaj* (companies), in His saying: ﴿Every time a company is cast into it﴾ [al-Mulk 8], and in al-A'raf He described them as *umam* (nations), in His saying: ﴿He will say: Enter into the Fire among nations that passed away before you, of jinn and humankind. Every time a nation enters, it curses its sister, until, when they have all overtaken one another therein, the last of them will say of the first of them…﴾ [al-A'raf 38].

He said in Fussilat: ﴿And the word has come to pass against them, among nations that passed away before them, of jinn and humankind. Indeed, they were losers﴾ [Fussilat 25]. And He said, exalted is He: ﴿This is a company rushing in with you. There is no welcome for them. Indeed, they will burn in the Fire﴾ [Sad 59].

Among the usages of *zumar* for what we have mentioned is the saying of the poet:

"And you see people going to his abode in groups, one group after another visiting him."

And the saying of the rajaz poet:

"Indeed the seekers have flocked to the gifts (al-suyub), until they came in groups upon groups."

The Almighty's saying: ﴿And their keepers will say to them: Did there not come to you messengers from among you, reciting to you the signs of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this day of yours? They will say: Yes, but the word of punishment has come due against the disbelievers﴾. We have already presented the verses clarifying this in Surat Bani Isra'il, in discussing His saying: ﴿And We would never punish until We send a messenger﴾ [al-Isra' 15].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 73:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Until, when they reach it and its gates are opened﴾. Here, may He be glorified and exalted, does not specify the number of its gates that are mentioned; but He did specify that in Surah al-Hijr, in His saying: ﴿And indeed, Hell is the promised place for them all. It has seven gates; for each gate there is a portion designated﴾ [al-Hijr: 43-44].

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿and its gates are opened﴾ — Nafi', Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr and Ibn 'Amir read it as (futtihat) with the letter ta' (doubled, indicating intensive emphasis).

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And its keepers will say to them, "Peace be upon you; you have done well, so enter it to abide therein."﴾ We have already mentioned the verses that clarify this in Surah al-Nahl, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those whom the angels take in death while they are good, saying, "Peace be upon you. Enter Paradise for what you used to do"﴾ [al-Nahl: 32].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 39, verse 74:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And they will say, "Praise be to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us and has caused us to inherit the earth, to dwell in the Garden wherever we will."﴾

In this noble verse, Allah, Majestic and Exalted, mentions that the people of Paradise, when they enter it and witness what it contains of bounty, praise their Lord and extol Him, and proclaim the truthfulness of His promise to them. Allah mentions this meaning in other verses of His Book, such as His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We will remove whatever rancor is in their breasts; beneath them rivers will flow. And they will say, "Praise be to Allah, who has guided us to this. And we would not have been guided if not that Allah had guided us. Certainly did the messengers of our Lord come with the truth." And they will be called, "This is Paradise, which you have been made to inherit for what you used to do."﴾ [Al-A'raf: 43]. And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And the companions of Paradise will call out to the companions of the Fire, "We have found true what our Lord promised us."﴾ up to the end of the verse [Al-A'raf: 44].

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence, which they will enter. They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their garments therein will be silk.﴾ ﴿And they will say, "Praise be to Allah, who has removed from us all grief. Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative."﴾ ﴿[He] who has settled us in the home of settlement from His bounty; no fatigue touches us therein, and no weariness touches us therein.﴾ [Fatir: 33–34].
